status: drafted via multi-agent workflow, adversarially fact-checked and corrected
notes: 1 John is almost entirely hortatory/thematic rather than narrative — there is no story being told, only pastoral teaching addressed to "my little children" and "beloved" — so 12 of its 13 tiers are law/theme type, the heaviest law-tier ratio of any book indexed so far (more even than Leviticus). The one person tier is the unnamed author himself ("The Eyewitness"), justified under the personally-embodied test because 1:1-4 is a first-person eyewitness claim ("which we have seen with our eyes... our hands have handled") and the whole letter is his own direct exhortation in his own voice — not him relaying someone else's teaching the way Matthew relays Jesus's discourses. Because of that, every law tier's "deliveredBy" points back to the author himself, not to a third party, which is a deliberate structural difference from the Gospel discourse-tier pattern. Jesus Christ is the letter's constant doctrinal subject (his incarnation, atoning blood, advocacy, sonship) but never acts within a narrated scene in this book, so per the personally-embodied-vs-pure-transmission test he gets a role:"named" entry rather than his own full manager tier (unlike every Gospel, where he does carry real scenes). Two accuracy flags: (1) the author is traditionally identified with John the Apostle/son of Zebedee (also credited with the Fourth Gospel and Revelation), but 1 John itself never names its writer — same caution already applied to the Gospel of John and Revelation, and there is a real naming-collision risk with John the Baptist and John Mark that must not be silently resolved. (2) 5:7-8 in the KJV includes the "three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost" clause (the "Comma Johanneum") — a well-documented textual-criticism question, since the clause is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts and most modern critical texts; it is indexed here because it is the actual printed KJV text this project uses, flagged descriptively as a scholarly question, not asserted as doctrinally settled. Cain (3:12) is a one-verse moral cross-reference to Genesis, not re-indexed as a character here since he carries no scene of his own in this book; logged in genealogyLists instead, consistent with how Matthew's OT genealogy references were handled. 4:7-8/4:16 ("God is love") is called out as the book's central thesis per the book-specific guidance and given a correspondingly full verse list in the "God Is Love" tier. CORRECTIONS APPLIED (adversarial fact-check pass): removed an interpretive/doctrinal gloss on 1 John 3:9 (draft rendered "doth not commit sin" as "does not make a practice of sin" — the specific "habitual sin" reconciliation with 1:8-10 is a common theological resolution but not what the literal KJV text says, so the entry now quotes the verse directly instead of asserting that reading); removed the same gloss pattern from the "Confidence Toward God" tier's purpose field, which had rendered 5:18 ("sinneth not"... "that wicked one toucheth him not") as "does not live in habitual sin" — now quotes the literal text instead of asserting a doctrinal resolution; added 1 John 3:19-21 to the "Love in Deed and in Truth" tier's verse list, since its purpose field already claimed the tier links love to "a confident heart before God" (the actual content of 3:19-21, e.g. "if our heart condemn us not, then have we confidence toward God") but no verse backing that claim had been cited; added 1 John 3:15 ("Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer") to the same tier's verse list, a standalone teaching statement directly adjacent to the surrounding verses the tier already covers (3:13-14, 3:16-18) that had been omitted with no cross-reference anywhere else.

scribeTiers.scribeName: Fathers, Young Men, and Little Children
Love in Deed and in Truth

characters.name: The Eyewitness (traditionally John the Apostle)
characters.perkNote: 1 John never names its own author. Traditional attribution to John the Apostle/son of Zebedee (also traditionally credited with the Fourth Gospel and Revelation) is a real textual/historical question, not a claim made by 1 John itself — flagged the same way as the Gospel of John and Revelation authorship. NAMING-COLLISION FLAG: at least three New Testament men are named John — John the Baptist, John the Apostle (son of Zebedee), and John Mark — this entry should never be silently merged with either of the other two.

genealogy.father: zebedee — traditional identification only (not stated anywhere in 1 John itself)

verses.note: Opens by claiming direct, physical eyewitness testimony of 'the Word of life' — heard, seen with his own eyes, looked upon, and handled with his own hands.
States that the eternal life he witnessed 'was manifested,' and that he bears witness of it and declares it.
States his purpose in writing: that readers may have fellowship with him, a fellowship that is 'with the Father, and with his Son Jesus Christ.'
States a second purpose: 'that your joy may be full.'

funFacts: Addresses his readers repeatedly and affectionately as 'my little children' (teknia) and 'beloved' (agapetoi) throughout the letter — a distinctive personal, pastoral voice rather than formal doctrinal argument.

Unlike Matthew's law tiers (deliveredBy: jesus, since Matthew is compiling Jesus's own discourses), every law tier in this book is deliveredBy this author himself — he is teaching in his own voice throughout, not relaying someone else's separate teaching.

characters.name: Jesus Christ

genealogy.father: not stated in 1 John itself — see the Gospel accounts (e.g. Matthew) for the virgin-birth genealogy

verses.note: Named as God's Son, with whom fellowship is shared.
'The blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin.'
Called 'an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.'
Called 'the propitiation for our sins... for the sins of the whole world.'
Denying 'that Jesus is the Christ' is defined as the mark of antichrist; denying the Son also means not having the Father.
The test for the Spirit of God: confessing 'that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh.'
God's love shown by sending 'his only begotten Son into the world' as the propitiation for sins.
'Whosoever shall confess that Jesus is the Son of God, God dwelleth in him.'
'Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God.'
Overcoming the world is defined as believing 'that Jesus is the Son of God.'
Called 'his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God, and eternal life.'

funFacts: Jesus never acts within a narrated scene anywhere in 1 John — no birth, ministry, or resurrection event is told here. He is discussed purely as the doctrinal subject of the author's teaching (his incarnation, atoning blood, advocacy, and sonship), which is why he gets a role:'named' entry here instead of his own full manager tier the way he does in every Gospel.

characters.name: Walking in the Light
characters.purpose: Teaches that fellowship with God requires walking in the light as God himself is light, that honest confession of sin (rather than the self-deceiving claim to have none) is the true posture of a believer, and that Jesus Christ's blood cleanses from sin while he also serves as advocate and propitiation when a believer does sin.

verses.note: 'God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.'
Claiming fellowship with God while walking in darkness is called a lie.
Walking in the light brings fellowship with one another and cleansing 'from all sin' by Christ's blood.
Claiming to have no sin is self-deception.
'If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.'
Claiming never to have sinned makes God 'a liar.'
Written 'that ye sin not' — but if any man sin, 'we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.'
Jesus Christ is 'the propitiation for our sins... also for the sins of the whole world.'

characters.name: Keeping His Commandments
characters.purpose: Teaches that true knowledge of God and abiding in him is proven by keeping his commandments, epitomized in an 'old yet new' commandment to love one's brother; loving a brother is equated with walking in the light, and hating a brother with remaining in darkness.

verses.note: 'Hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments.'
Claiming to know God while not keeping his commandments makes one 'a liar.'
Abiding in God means walking as Christ walked.
Describes the commandment (to love) as both an 'old commandment' already held and a 'new commandment,' since 'the darkness is past, and the true light now shineth.'
Claiming to be in the light while hating one's brother means still being 'in darkness.'
'He that loveth his brother abideth in the light.'
Hating one's brother leaves a person walking in darkness, not knowing where he goes, 'because that darkness hath blinded his eyes.'

characters.name: Fathers, Young Men, and Little Children
characters.scribeTier: Fathers, Young Men, and Little Children
characters.purpose: A brief poetic passage of assurance addressed in turn to three groups of believers at different stages of spiritual maturity, affirming forgiveness of sins, knowledge of God 'from the beginning,' and victory over 'the wicked one' through the abiding word of God.

verses.note: 'I write unto you, little children, because your sins are forgiven you for his name's sake.'
Addresses 'fathers' (who have known him 'from the beginning') and 'young men' (who 'have overcome the wicked one').
Restates and expands the address, adding that the young men are strong and 'the word of God abideth in you.'

characters.name: Love Not the World
characters.purpose: Warns against loving 'the world' — defined specifically as 'the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life' — and contrasts the world's passing away with the permanence of one who does the will of God.

verses.note: 'Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.'
Names the three components of worldly desire: lust of the flesh, lust of the eyes, and pride of life.
'The world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.'

characters.name: The Many Antichrists
characters.purpose: Warns that 'it is the last time' and that many antichrists — false teachers who deny that Jesus is the Christ and who 'went out from us' — have already appeared; reassures believers of an 'unction from the Holy One' that teaches them truth directly, and urges them to let what they heard 'from the beginning' remain in them.

verses.note: 'It is the last time: and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists.'
The antichrists 'went out from us, but they were not of us.'
'Ye have an unction from the Holy One, and ye know all things.'
Defines antichrist as 'he that denieth that Jesus is the Christ... that denieth the Father and the Son.'
Urges what was 'heard from the beginning' to remain in them, promising eternal life in return.
'The anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you, and ye need not that any man teach you.'

characters.name: Children of God
characters.purpose: Contrasts children of God with children of the devil; teaches the hope of one day being made like Christ 'when he shall appear,' and that sin (defined as 'the transgression of the law') is incompatible with abiding in Christ, while practicing righteousness and loving one's brother are the visible marks of God's children.

verses.note: 'Every one that doeth righteousness is born of him.'
'Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God.'
'When he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.'
Defines sin as 'the transgression of the law.'
Christ 'was manifested to take away our sins; and in him is no sin.'
'He that committeth sin is of the devil... the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil.'
'Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; for his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God.'
'In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother.'

characters.name: Love in Deed and in Truth
characters.scribeTier: Love in Deed and in Truth
characters.purpose: Expands on the command to love one another as 'the message that ye heard from the beginning,' using Cain as a negative cautionary example (a one-verse cross-reference, not indexed as a character in this book — see genealogyLists) and stating that hatred of a brother is itself a form of murder, and teaches that real love is proven by sacrificial action — being willing 'to lay down our lives for the brethren' and sharing material goods with a brother in need — 'not in word... but in deed and in truth,' linking such love to a confident heart before God (an assurance that holds even when 'our own heart condemn us') and to answered prayer.

verses.note: 'This is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.'
Cites Cain, 'who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother,' as the negative counter-example.
'Marvel not, my brethren, if the world hate you.'
'We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren.'
'Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.'
Christ laying down his life for believers is the model: 'we ought also to lay down our lives for the brethren.'
Withholding material help from a brother in need calls into question whether 'the love of God' truly dwells in a person.
'Let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth.'
'Hereby we know that we are of the truth, and shall assure our hearts before him. For if our heart condemn us, God is greater than our heart, and knoweth all things.'
'If our heart condemn us not, then have we confidence toward God.'
Keeping God's commandments — summarized as believing on the name of his Son Jesus Christ and loving one another — is tied to receiving whatever is asked of him in prayer.

characters.name: Trying the Spirits
characters.purpose: Instructs believers not to 'believe every spirit,' but to 'try the spirits whether they are of God,' giving a concrete doctrinal test — confessing that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh — to distinguish the Spirit of God/spirit of truth from the spirit of antichrist/spirit of error.

verses.note: 'Believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world.'
'Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God.'
Every spirit that does not confess this 'is not of God: and this is that spirit of antichrist.'
'Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world.'
'Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.'

characters.name: God Is Love
characters.purpose: The letter's central theological statement — that God's very nature is love, demonstrated concretely in sending his only begotten Son so that believers 'might live through him' and have their sins propitiated; because God loved first, believers are commanded to love one another, God's love is 'perfected'/made complete in that mutual love, and 'perfect love casteth out fear,' particularly fear of judgment.

verses.note: 'Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God.'
'He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.'
God's love toward believers was manifested by sending 'his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him.'
'Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins.'
'Beloved, if God so loved us, we ought also to love one another.'
'If we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us.'
'God is love; and he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God, and God in him.'
'There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment.'
'We love him, because he first loved us.'
Claiming to love God while hating one's brother makes a person 'a liar.'
'This commandment have we from him, That he who loveth God love his brother also.'

funFacts: 4:8 and 4:16 both state 'God is love' — the only two verses in the entire Bible that phrase it this exact way, given real thematic weight in this tier per the book-specific brief.

characters.name: Overcoming the World
characters.purpose: Teaches that faith that Jesus is the Christ, love for God, and love for God's children are all inseparably bound together, and that this faith itself is 'the victory that overcometh the world.'

verses.note: 'Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God.'
'This is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.'
'Whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.'
'Who is he that overcometh the world, but he that believeth that Jesus is the Son of God?'

characters.name: The Three Witnesses
characters.purpose: Presents the testimony establishing belief in the Son — 'the Spirit, and the water, and the blood' bearing witness on earth (with verses 7-8's added heavenly-witness clause about the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost being a well-documented textual-criticism question, since it is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts, noted here descriptively rather than asserted as settled) — concluding that God's own witness concerning his Son is greater than any human testimony, and that this testimony is the basis of eternal life.

verses.note: 'This is he that came by water and blood, even Jesus Christ... And it is the Spirit that beareth witness, because the Spirit is truth.'

'There are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one' — KJV text; a widely-noted textual variant (the 'Comma Johanneum') absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts and most modern critical texts, flagged here as a real scholarly question, not a doctrinal assertion by this project.
'There are three that bear witness in earth, the Spirit, and the water, and the blood: and these three agree in one.'
'If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater.'
'This is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.'
'He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.'
States the purpose of the whole letter: 'that ye may know that ye have eternal life... and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God.'

characters.name: Confidence Toward God
characters.purpose: Closes the letter with practical pastoral instruction — confidence in prayer offered according to God's will, intercession for a brother caught in sin (distinguishing 'a sin unto death' from sin 'not unto death' without further specifying what that sin is), the statement that whosoever is born of God 'sinneth not' because 'that wicked one toucheth him not,' and a final short warning to 'keep yourselves from idols.'

verses.note: 'This is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us.'
Distinguishes 'a sin which is not unto death' (for which one should pray for a brother) from 'a sin unto death,' which he does not instruct prayer for — without specifying further what that sin is.
'Whosoever is born of God sinneth not... and that wicked one toucheth him not.'
'We know that we are of God, and the whole world lieth in wickedness.'
'We know that the Son of God is come, and hath given us an understanding, that we may know him that is true.'
Final line of the letter: 'Little children, keep yourselves from idols. Amen.'

genealogyLists.note: Bulk or deliberately-unresolved references, kept out of the character list above.

cain_reference.note: Cited by name as a negative moral example ('Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother') within the Love in Deed and in Truth tier's teaching against hatred of a brother. Cain is already indexed as a full character in the Genesis character index; not re-indexed here since he carries no scene of his own within 1 John itself, only a single-verse illustrative cross-reference — same handling as Matthew's bulk OT genealogy references.

the_elder_title_note.ref: 2 John 1:1 / 3 John 1:1 (for cross-reference only, not part of this book)
the_elder_title_note.note: The author of the Johannine epistles calls himself 'the elder' in 2 John and 3 John, but 1 John itself never uses this or any other self-designation — flagged here for continuity when 2 John/3 John are indexed, since the same 'author_1_john' identity question will recur there.
